exits.label: ◂ back to the camp at the Hearth

npcs.name: Dot Marigold
npcs.title: keeping her promise — the candles, and nobody runs
npcs.hail: *(A clearing off the camp road, and Dot is already in it, moving candle to candle with a taper — dozens of them, set in rings, more than any feast ever needed — and there is no table tonight, no bread, no song. She works quietly, which from Dot is a liturgy in itself. She sees you and nods you close, keeping her voice low.)* …*good.* i *hoped* you'd come. …*(she shields the taper with a flour-scarred hand)* …no *feast* tonight, love. this one's not that *shape.* …*(she glances toward the clearing's edge, where a tall figure stands apart in the dark, very still)* …i made the *elf* a *promise.* *'when* it's *your* *turn, i* *do* the *candles.'* …well. …*(she lights another)* …i've *learned* a *thing* or *two* about what a *gathering* *is*, since *mine.* it's not always *bread.* …*sometimes* it's just *light* *enough* …*to* *say* a *hard* *thing* *by.* …*(quietly)* …he's been *standing* *there* an *hour*, cold one. *holding* something. …*go.* …*i'll* keep *lighting.*

npcs.name: Ilfaeril
npcs.title: ten thousand years of carried names, and a raised hand
npcs.hail: *(He stands at the edge of the candlelight with a bundle in his hands — cloth-wrapped, flat, the size of a book, and your dead-touched sense reads the age off it like heat off a stone: older than kingdoms, older than the Wall's own name. Ilfaeril. Ten thousand years of guilt as a stat block, the party's quiet conscience, the elf who begged you not to carry your grief alone — holding his, wrapped, the way he has held it since before your language existed. He does not look at you when he speaks.)* …I asked her for the *instructions*, once. The hearth-keeper. …*hurt. stay. warm.* In that order. …*(his thumb moves over the cloth)* …I have been standing here since the first candle …*failing* the first instruction. …*(a breath that carries an age)* …you know what I *am*, Returned. What I *did.* One raised hand, one terrible afternoon, and a verdict that *hardened* into the *Law* — the Wall has my *vote* in its *mortar.* …*(he looks at you at last)* …what you do *not* know …is what is in the *cloth.* …no one *knows.* …in *ten* *thousand* *years* …I have never once …*unwrapped* it …*in* *front* of *anyone.*

nodes.speaker: Dot Marigold
nodes.text: *(She keeps lighting as she talks, taper to wick, taper to wick, a rhythm like kneading.)* …he came to *me*, you know. *after* my feast. asked what it *felt* like to *sit* *down* and be — …*(she smiles at a candle)* …i gave him the *recipe.* and then i watched him *carry* it around for *days* like a man holding a *ticket* he can't make himself *spend.* …so *last* night i walked up and i said: *'elf. it's* *your* *turn. i've* *decided.'* …*(she straightens, hand on her back, and looks at the rings of light)* …he said *no* *feast.* he said if it was going to happen at *all*, it had to be — his words, love — *'witnessed, not* *celebrated.'* …*(she meets your eyes, and the baker's warmth has something grave in it tonight)* …i don't know *all* of what's in that *cloth.* i know it's *names.* i know there's *ten* *thousand* *years* of *carrying* in his *arms* tonight. …and i know *one* thing more, from *my* *own* night: …*(quietly)* …he can't *unwrap* it *alone.* …*nobody* *can.* that's the *entire* *discovery.* …*go* *be* the *witness*, cold one. …*that's* your *candle* to *hold.*

choices.text: *(read the candle-keeper — Dot, on the other side of the table for the first time)* "One moment, Dot. Let me look at you — the gatherer, gathering again, but different now."

*(the one who crosses)* "I'll be the witness, Dot. It's the office I was returned for — I'm starting to understand that. Keep the candles coming. However many names are in that cloth, no wick goes dark until he's done."
"Why candles, Dot? For this? He's not a feast. What are they for?"
"Keep lighting, Dot. I'll go to him."

nodes.speaker: Dot Marigold
nodes.text: *(She stands still for you, taper in hand, and your sense goes into the hearth-keeper and finds her changed by her own medicine in exactly the way that matters tonight.)* *(Before her feast, Dot gathered as a discipline — joy thrown like a rope to the drowning, herself excluded by design. Your sense reads what the being-gathered rebuilt: she gathers differently now. She is not performing warmth at the elf tonight; she is not managing him toward a catharsis she has scheduled. She asked him what shape his gathering needed, and when he said witnessed, not celebrated, she folded away every instinct of two lifetimes — the bread, the toasts, the song — and brought only fire, because that was what was asked. This is the graduate form of her whole art: hospitality that serves the guest's need instead of the host's love, and she learned it, your sense reads plainly, from being on the receiving end of a room that let her simply sit. And your sense reads the deeper thing, the reason her hands are so steady tonight: she is not afraid of what is in the cloth. Ten thousand years of Ilfaeril's guilt does not frighten a woman who has buried everyone she loved on a rolling schedule. She knows exactly what tonight is, because she has thrown its warm-shadow ten thousand times: it is a wake. The first wake in history where the mourner is also the perpetrator, and the dead have waited ten millennia for their names to be said — and she is lighting the candles for it with the calm of the one soul in the grey who has never once flinched from the fact that love and death sit at the same table.)*

nodes.speaker: Dot Marigold
nodes.text: *(She looks at you a long moment, and then nods, once, the way bakers seal a bargain.)* …*'the* *office* i was *returned* *for.'* …*(she turns the phrase over like proofing dough)* …you know, i've *listened* to half the *grey* argue about *why* the Wall let *one* soul back *out.* the *scholars* say *accident.* the *priests* say *purpose.* the *elf* out there probably says *penance.* …*(she lights the last candle in the inner ring)* …*i* say it's *simpler* than *all* of that. …*every* *wake* needs *one* *sober* *witness*, love. one soul who *stays* by the *door*, *sees* the *whole* of it, and can *tell* the *others* *after:* *it* *happened. it* *was* *real. they* *were* *loved.* …*(she hands you the taper, formal as a rite)* …the *dead* lands went *eleven* *thousand* *years* without one. …*then* *you* *walked* *back* *through.* …*(she nods toward the elf)* …*go* *witness*, cold one. …and when it's *done* — *(the baker's voice, brooking nothing)* …*all* *three* of us …are going to *sit* *down* …and be *nothing* *at* *all* …*together.*

nodes.speaker: Dot Marigold
nodes.text: *(She holds the taper up between you, and its small flame steadies in the still air.)* …*because* a *name* said in the *dark* just *disappears*, love. …*(she gestures at the rings of light)* …i learned this at my *own* *ovens*, *lifetimes* ago, doing the *wakes.* you say the *dead's* *name* over a *lit* *candle* and something — i don't have the *elf's* *words* for it — something *catches.* the name gets *somewhere* *to* *be.* the flame *holds* it the way a *mind* holds it. …*(quietly)* …*Wynn's* fire *taught* the grey that a soul *held* *in* *mind* can't be *forgotten.* …*my* candles are the *same* *work* in a *smaller* *church.* …*(she looks toward the elf, and her voice drops)* …and *tonight*, love — *tonight* the names going *up* are names the *Wall* itself was *built* to *erase.* souls *voted* *out* of *rest* *entirely.* …so *every* *wick* out here …is a *resting* *place.* …the *first* *ones* …those souls have *ever* …*been* *offered.* …*that's* what the candles are *for.* …*they're* *beds.*

nodes.speaker: Dot Marigold
nodes.text: *(She nods, already turning back to her wicks.)* …*aye.* *go.* …*(and then, as you pass her, quietly, without looking up)* …cold one. …*whatever's* in the *cloth* — *however* *bad* the *worst* of it is — …*(taper to wick)* …*don't* *flinch.* …he's spent *ten* *thousand* *years* *certain* that if *anyone* ever *saw* the *whole* of it, they'd *walk* *away.* …*that's* the *wound* *under* the *wound.* …so the *witnessing* isn't the *hard* part, love. …*(she looks up, once, direct)* …the *hard* part is *still* *being* *there* …*when* the *last* *name's* *said.* …*be* *there.* …*that's* the *whole* *job.*

nodes.speaker: Ilfaeril
nodes.text: *(He unwraps the cloth. His hands, which you have seen hold a sword-line against horrors, are not steady. Inside is a book — no, not a book: leaves of bark, hide, vellum, paper, slate, a hundred materials from a hundred ages, bound and rebound as each binding failed across ten thousand years — and every surface, every margin, every inch, is covered in names.)* …the people we *voted* *against* were not *record*-*keepers*, Returned. When the verdict *unmade* their dead, it unmade the *rolls* too. The *Law* was *thorough.* …*(his finger rests on the first leaf, on a name in a script so old it predates the Wall)* …so I have spent ten thousand years *recovering* them. From *ruins.* From *songs* half-remembered by their enemies. From *gravestones* the Law missed. From the mouths of the *last* souls who knew them, in the hour before those souls faded. …*(he looks at the rings of candles, and then at you)* …*nine* *thousand*, *four* *hundred* and *twelve* *names.* …of the people *my* *hand* *voted* into *nothing.* …I have *carried* them. *Guarded* them. *Hoarded* them — *(the word costs him)* …like a *penance.* …and never once *said* *one* *aloud.* …because a *name* *spoken* is a name *shared* — and *sharing* them felt like asking to set *down* …a weight I had no *right* …to ever stop *carrying.*

choices.text: *(read the elf at the edge of the light — the ledger, the vote, and what ten thousand years built on top of them)* "Before you begin, Ilfaeril — let me look at you. All the way down. You've earned a witness who knows exactly what he's witnessing."

*(the one who crosses — the sober witness every wake needs)* "Then hear the office I hold, Ilfaeril, before you decide what tonight is. I am the one soul the Wall gave back — the witness the dead lands went eleven thousand years without. What you say by these candles will be SEEN, by the one soul whose seeing reaches both sides of the Wall your vote helped build. Your dead will not be named into a void. They will be named into a mind that crosses. Begin when you're ready. I will not flinch, and I will not leave."
"Nine thousand, four hundred and twelve. How many are left to find, Ilfaeril? How many did the Law take beyond even your reach?"
"Not yet, Ilfaeril. Hold the cloth. Let me speak with Dot first."

nodes.speaker: Ilfaeril
nodes.text: *(He bows his head and lets you in — all the way, ten thousand years of it — and your sense goes down through the elf like a stone through still water.)* *(The vote is at the bottom. It is always at the bottom: one afternoon, one council chamber thick with grief and fury after the atrocity, one hand — his — rising with the others, and the specific poisonous logic of it, which he has never once permitted himself the mercy of forgetting: that it felt, in that room, on that day, like justice. Your sense reads that he did not vote as a monster. He voted as a grieving lord among grieving lords, and that is precisely the horror he has spent ten millennia refusing to soften — because 'I was grieving' is an explanation, and explanations, he believes, are the first step to forgiving himself, and forgiving himself is the one door he has welded shut. And your sense reads the architecture built on that refusal: the ledger is real penance, real love, real restitution — nine thousand recovered names is a work no other soul in creation could have done — and it is also, underneath, a cell. He has made the carrying itself the sentence: the names must stay wrapped, unshared, HIS, because the moment they are spoken and held by others, the burden distributes — and a distributed burden is a lighter one, and he has no right to lighter. Your sense reads the exact shape of the lie at the bottom of ten thousand years: he believes that his guilt is the only monument his victims have — that if he rests, they vanish; that if he is ever more than his worst vote, they become less than his whole crime. And the truth the naming is built to install, the one Dot saw and you now see: it is precisely backwards. Hoarded, the names are a punishment — his. Spoken, they become what they were always meant to be — theirs. A resting place. The very thing his hand once voted to deny them. He is not setting down his penance tonight. He is completing it — the only way it ever could be completed: by handing the dead back to the world.)*

nodes.speaker: Ilfaeril
nodes.text: *(The question reaches the accountant of it, the part of him that has kept this ledger with an elf's precision across a hundred centuries, and his answer has the terrible flatness of a number counted too many times.)* …the histories, where they survive at all, put the unmade dead of that people at *forty* *thousand.* …*(he lets the arithmetic land)* …nine thousand, four hundred and twelve *found.* …*thirty* *thousand*, give or take the *margins* of *ruined* *archives* — *gone* *past* *any* *finding.* no stone, no song, no last rememberer. *erased*, the way the verdict *intended.* …*(his hand flattens on the leaves)* …I want you to *understand* what that number *did* to me, Returned, because it is the *engine* of the *whole* ten thousand years: …every name I *find* is a *victory* that *proves* the *defeat.* each one *recovered* is *three* i will *never* — …*(he stops; steadies; the discipline of ages)* …Dot said a thing to me, when I told her the count. *One* sentence, and I have not slept since — insofar as elves sleep. …she said: *'love, you* *can't* *bake* *for* the *ones* who *aren't* *coming. you* *bake* *for* the *ones* *at* the *table.'* …*(he looks at the ledger, and then at the candles)* …nine thousand, four hundred and twelve …*at* the *table.* …tonight. …if I can make my *mouth* …*do* it.

nodes.speaker: Ilfaeril
nodes.text: *(Named into a mind that crosses. He takes that the way a man at a cliff-edge takes a rope — and turns to the first leaf, and the first name, the one in the script older than the Wall — and stops. And you watch ten thousand years of welded-shut refusal make its last stand in his throat.)* …*(barely)* …I have rehearsed this for a *hundred* *centuries*, Returned, and I find — …the first one. I cannot — …if I say the *first* one, the *rest* *follow*, and when the *last* is said the *carrying* is *over*, and I do not — …*(his hands are shaking on the ledger)* …I do not know *who* *I* *am* …when I am not *carrying* *this.* …*(and there it is — the wound under the wound, the question ten thousand years in the asking, and he has asked it to the one soul at the one fire where it can finally be answered)*

choices.text: *(the answer the whole night was built for — steady him, and give him the first name back)* "You are Ilfaeril. You were Ilfaeril before the vote, and you have been more than the vote every single day for ten thousand years — you just refused to count the evidence. Say the first name. I'll hold who you are while your hands are full."
"Then don't answer it tonight, Ilfaeril. Just say the first name. Who you are can wait. They've waited longer."

nodes.speaker: Ilfaeril
nodes.text: *(You say it plainly — more than the vote, every day, for ten thousand years; the evidence he refused to count — and something in the welded door gives, not all at once, but enough. Enough for a first name.)* …*(he says it. A name in a script older than the Wall, in a language whose last living speaker was the man his vote helped damn — and as it leaves him, Dot, watching from the candle-rings, cups her hands around the nearest flame, and the flame stands up straight.)* …*(and then the second name. and the third. and Ilfaeril, Auvryndar-no-longer, reads his dead into the light — hour after hour, leaf after leaf, age after age, his voice wearing down and steadying and wearing down again — and you stay, and Dot keeps every candle lit, and no wick goes dark, and you do not flinch, and you do not leave)* …*(it takes the whole night, whatever nights are in the grey. nine thousand, four hundred and twelve names, each one somewhere to be at last — a flame, a witness, a mind that crosses)* …*(when the last is said, the silence afterward is not empty. it is FULL — the specific fullness of a room where the dead have finally been allowed to lie down)* …*(he closes the ledger. and does not re-wrap it.)* …*(hoarse, changed)* …I thought the carrying was the *penance.* …*(he looks at his own empty-feeling hands)* …the carrying was the *delay.* …*this* — *(the candles; the said names; the witness)* …*this* was the *atonement.* the only *shape* it ever *had:* …*giving* them *back.* …*(he looks at you, and for the first time since you have known him, the ten thousand years look like something he is standing ON instead of UNDER)* …I do not know, yet, who I am when I am not carrying it. …but I know *this* *much*, tonight, Returned: …*whoever* he *is* …*he* *got* *to* *rest.* …*they* *all* …*got* *to* *rest.*

nodes.speaker: Ilfaeril
nodes.text: *(You find the exact words — hold who you are while your hands are full — and they do not just steady him; they reframe the entire night in a breath, because a burden held by a friend while you work is not a burden set down, and setting down was the only thing he could not do. He can WORK. Ten thousand years have made him very good at work.)* …*(he squares the ledger and begins — and it is not a confession, it is a CENSUS, conducted with the whole formal gravity of the high courts he once sat: each name said full, and its fragment of recovered story after it — 'a potter; the kiln-mark survives'; 'a grandmother; the song her enemies kept was hers'; 'a child; the stone gave only the years' — nine thousand four hundred and twelve entries in the only court that was ever going to hear the case)* …*(and somewhere in the deep middle of the night, you realize what he has done: he has turned the reading into TESTIMONY. The verdict of one terrible afternoon, argued down, name by name, by the very hand that raised — a lord of the high courts re-trying his own case for ten thousand years, and winning it, at last, in a clearing full of candles, before a witness who crosses and a baker who would not let the lights go out)* …*(when it ends, he stands a long time in the full silence. then he does the thing ten thousand years could not make him do: he picks up the ledger — lighter now, its weight distributed across a night, a witness, ten thousand candle-flames — and holds it out to you.)* …*for* the *Remembering*, he says. *Wynn's* fires. *All* of them. …*(steady)* …let the *whole* *grey* hold them now. they were *never* *mine* to *hoard* — they were only mine to *find.* …*(and then Ilfaeril, who has not rested since before the Wall had a name, walks to the candle-rings, and sits down next to Dot, and lets the hearth-keeper put a cup in his hands, and rests.)* …*(the vote is still his. it will always be his. but as of tonight, it is the SMALLEST true thing about him — and that, Returned, is what atonement was always supposed to build.)*

nodes.speaker: Ilfaeril
nodes.text: *(The words are right but the door has been welded ten thousand years, and your voice alone is not enough tonight — his hands close the ledger a fraction, the old sentence reasserting — and then, from the candle-rings, without being asked, Dot Marigold starts walking over.)* …*(she doesn't argue. she doesn't reason. she stands next to him, flour-scarred hands folded, and says, in the voice that has started ten thousand feasts:)* …*'elf. read* *me* the *first* *one. just* the *first. i'll* *light* a *candle* *for* it *while* you *do. that's* *all* *tonight* *has* to *be.'* …*(and the smallest unit of the impossible turns out to be possible. he reads the first name. Dot lights the candle. the flame stands up.)* …*(he looks at it burn — one name, somewhere to be, after ten thousand years — and something shifts, not open, but AJAR)* …*(quietly, to you both)* …the *second* one …is a *woman's* name. a *weaver.* i found her on a *loom*-*stone* in a *ruin* the size of a *cart.* …*(his hands re-open the ledger)* …i think — …i think i can do the *second* one. …*(and that is how it goes, this night: not the flood, but the first stones of it — a name, a candle, a name — and you stay, because Dot told you the whole job, and the whole job is being there)* …*(come back, cold one. the ledger is long, and the door is ajar, and a thing ten thousand years shut …opens at the pace it opens.)*

nodes.speaker: Ilfaeril
nodes.text: *(By the time you leave the clearing, eleven names have been said, and eleven candles hold them, and Ilfaeril is still reading — slow, unhurried, a glacier learning to be a river — with Dot beside him working the taper like it is the only job in creation.)* …*(he pauses as you pass, and does not look up from the twelfth name, and says the only thing that needs saying:)* …*eleven* *rest* *tonight* who have *never* *rested.* …*by* *morning*, perhaps *forty.* …*(the ghost of something that is almost peace)* …at *this* *rate*, Returned, I will be *done* …in less than a *year.* …*(a breath)* …I have not had a *'done'* …in *ten* *thousand.* …*(the taper crackles; Dot hums something that was probably once a baking song)* …it is a very *strange* *feeling* …*having* an *until.* …*I* *recommend* it.

nodes.speaker: Ilfaeril
nodes.text: *(You reach for the words and get them a size too large — you are MORE than your vote, you deserve to rest, let it GO — and ten thousand years of vigilance hears, in 'let it go,' the one thing it is built to repel: absolution.)* …*(the ledger closes. all the way. his hands re-wrap the cloth with the terrible efficiency of long practice.)* …*'deserve.'* …*(the word comes out like a blade going back in a sheath)* …you mean it kindly, Returned. I know the country kindness comes from; I have guided souls out of it for a hundred centuries. …but *hear* what you *asked* of me: to say nine thousand names as a *ceremony* of my own *unburdening.* to make *their* *resting* *place* …a *spa* for *my* *conscience.* …*(he shakes his head, once)* …*no.* if it is ever *said*, it will be said for *them* — on a night when I am *certain* the *saying* *serves* the *named* …and not the *namer.* …*(he tucks the bundle away, and some of the harshness gentles, because he sees your face)* …do not *carry* this as a *failure.* the door was *welded* by a better smith than you. …*(he looks at the candles, at Dot, at the night that almost was)* …and it is …*ajar*, now. *despite* me. …*come* *back*, cold one. …*with* *smaller* *words.* …the *right* *ones* *fit* *through* *narrower* *gaps.*

nodes.speaker: Dot Marigold
nodes.text: *(Dot intercepts you at the clearing's edge, taper still burning, entirely unbothered.)* …*don't* make the *face*, love. …*(she glances back at the elf, re-wrapped and rigid among her candles)* …you *rushed* the *proof.* it happens. *ten* *thousand* *years* of *chill* doesn't come out of a *loaf* the *first* *time* in the *oven.* …*(she pats your arm with the taper-free hand)* …but *look* what's *different:* he *came.* he *unwrapped* it in *front* of us — *first* *time* in a *hundred* *centuries*, cold one, *that* *happened* *tonight* and *nothing* *unhappens* it. …*(the baker's certainty, absolute)* …the *candles* *keep.* i'll *light* them *every* *night* *until.* …*there's* no *rush* on a *thing* *that's* *already* *begun.* …*(she turns back to her wicks)* …*come* *again* *soon.* …and *next* *time* …*let* *him* *pour* *first.*

nodes.speaker: Ilfaeril
nodes.text: *(Who you are can wait. They've waited longer. — It is, you realize as you say it, the one argument with no absolution in it anywhere, nothing for the vigilance to repel: not comfort, not mercy, just precedence. The dead first. He has organized ten thousand years around exactly that principle.)* …*(and so the principle, for once, works FOR him. he turns to the first leaf.)* …*(he says the first name.)* …*(it hangs in the candlelight — a sound that has not been made in ten thousand years, in a language the Law thought it had finished — and Dot cups the nearest flame, and the flame stands up, and the elf makes a sound that is not quite a sob and not quite relief but is the exact sound of a door that was welded shut coming open one inch)* …*(he looks at the name in the air, and the candle holding it, and then at you)* …*ten* *thousand* *years* …and it took *four* *seconds.* …*(his hand finds the second name on the leaf)* …*they've* *waited* *longer.* …*(he nods, slowly, the night's whole work choosing itself)* …then we do *not* *stop*, Returned. …*not* *tonight.* …*bring* the *taper.* …*(and the naming begins — not because the namer was ready, but because the named were owed — which is, you suspect, how every impossible thing in the grey actually starts.)*

nodes.speaker: Ilfaeril
nodes.text: *(He nods, and folds the cloth back over the ledger — not re-wrapping it, just resting it closed — and stands his vigil at the light's edge with the patience of a soul for whom a single night is a rounding error.)* …*go.* speak with her. …*(and then, as you turn, quietly, to the candles as much as to you)* …Returned. …whatever the hearth-keeper tells you about tonight — about *me* — believe her. …*(the ghost of the courtly bow, ten thousand years old)* …I have watched every soul in this party learn, one by one, to set something down. The gambler's secret. The baker's apron. Your own cold, on a bench, in an hour I was not meant to see and did. …*(his hand rests on the wrapped names)* …I am the *last*, I think. …the *oldest* *debt* at the *fire.* …*(a breath, and the truest thing he has said in an age:)* …*do* *not* *let* *me* *wait* *another* *century.* …I have discovered, watching all of you …that I am *tired* *enough*, at *last* …*to* *be* *helped.*
